title: The Value a Cancellation Share Is Taken On Where a Package Has Been Paid For
content:
What the party has actually put into a package sold under Wanderlane's Vacation Package Products, and what has been priced onto its ledger beyond the package price, decide the value a cancellation share is taken on. The money the party has put into the package is every deposit and every instalment taken on it; the components priced onto it are the component lines standing on its ledger.

**Paid up, with components priced beyond the price.** Where the money the party has put into the package reaches the package price and the package ledger carries components priced onto it beyond that price — 1 or more such lines, coming to more than nothing — the penalised value is the package price together with the components priced onto the ledger, the suppliers having been paid for both.

**Part paid.** Where the money the party has put into the package falls short of the package price and some money has been put in — more than nothing — the penalised value is the money the party has actually put in.

**Otherwise.** Where the party has put nothing at all into the package, or has paid up to the package price with no component priced onto the ledger beyond it, the penalised value is not varied under this note.

## Worked on hypothetical particulars

A package priced at 5,000.00 USD whose deposits and instalments come to 5,000.00 USD, its ledger carrying components of 640.00 USD: the money put in reaches the package price and components stand beyond it, so the penalised value is 5,640.00 USD.

The same package whose deposits and instalments come to 1,800.00 USD falls short of the package price, and some money has been put in, so the penalised value is 1,800.00 USD.

The same package with nothing at all put into it: the penalised value is not varied here.
